forecast.desc: After the driest June in over a decade (~40% deficit), a strong July recovery (+4% vs normal) narrowed the seasonal deficit to ~12%. IMD's August–September outlook is below-normal to near-normal; August pegged at 97% of LPA (±9%).
forecast.inference: The season has proven more resilient than the June collapse implied — but not out of the woods. July's low-pressure systems and depressions drove a strong recovery that cut the seasonal deficit from ~40% to ~12%, and IMD now pegs August near 97% of LPA. The distribution has improved from the July vintage's 60% deficient-probability, but a below-normal seasonal total remains the central case given the strengthening El Niño. The whole-season outcome now hinges on August–September holding near IMD's forecast rather than relapsing.

seasonal.desc: June and July were the most contrasting months of the season. June was the driest in over a decade; July outperformed. The El Niño suppression the spring anticipated for late season is the risk into August–September.
seasonal.inference: The season inverted the textbook Super El Niño script twice over. It suppressed rainfall early (a severe June, contrary to the 'monsoon escapes the peak' thesis), then July recovered strongly against expectations as low-pressure systems formed. The back-half risk now re-emerges: as El Niño intensifies toward its autumn peak, August–September face renewed suppression pressure, and IMD's below-normal call for the second half reflects exactly that. The season is a genuine tug-of-war between synoptic-scale recovery and the strengthening ENSO signal.

onset.desc: IMD declared Kerala onset on June 4 — three days later than the June 1 normal, and against pre-season forecasts of an early arrival. Onset stalled at both ends for nearly two weeks.
onset.inference: The late onset was the leading edge of the June collapse — the same weak circulation that delayed arrival produced the ~40% June deficit. Onset stalled at both ends for close to two weeks, and the arrival never became the season's highlight. It is a useful reminder that onset timing is only weakly correlated with the seasonal total: the season went on to recover sharply in July despite the poor start, then faces renewed El Niño pressure into the back half.

reservoir.desc: Live storage across major reservoirs vs the 10-year average. The July recovery has helped replenish storage after the June drawdown.
reservoir.inference: The buffer that made this a price story rather than a supply-collapse story has held and improved through the July recovery. Storage sits comfortably above the ten-year average, and the sharp July rains eased the June drawdown. Supply is buffered; the live risk remains price transmission on the crops hit by June's deficit and the uneven distribution — pulses and oilseeds sowing ran behind, and a below-normal August–September would keep upward pressure on food inflation into the Oct–Dec window.

regional.desc: The June–July swing was dramatic and uneven. Central India flipped from ~50% deficit to ~33% excess; the northwest recovered; east/northeast and the south peninsula lagged throughout.
regional.inference: The regional picture reorganised completely between June and July. Central India — the core rain-fed belt and the worst-hit region in June (~50% deficit) — swung to ~33% July excess and now carries a small seasonal surplus, the single biggest positive of the recovery. The northwest similarly rebounded. The persistent laggards are east/northeast India and the south peninsula, which barely improved across both months and remain the deficit concentration heading into the El Niño-pressured back half.
